items.physical_scope: Formal coefficientwise gauge fixing and local renormalization data for the adopted pure SU(2) Yang–Mills model; it constructs no continuum functional measure or continuum theory.
items.statement:
Use the adopted pure $SU(2)$ Yang–Mills model: $G=SU(2)$, $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{su}(2)$, the selected smooth right-principal bundle sector has no matter fields, and the positive invariant form is $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ with $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$ for $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$, extended bilinearly to the graded coefficient algebra. Work in a nonempty local trivialization chart of the selected bundle over oriented, time-oriented Minkowski space with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and coordinates $x^0=t$ in natural units $c=\hbar=1$. With the alternating wedge–Lie bracket fixed by the principal-curvature supplier, write $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$. The adopted Lorentzian gauge action is $S_0[A]=-(2g_{\rm YM}^2)^{-1}\int\kappa(F_A\wedge *F_A)$, with fixed positive dimensionless $g_{\rm YM}$. In the perturbative formulas $A_\mu$ has canonical engineering dimension $1$ and $g_{\rm YM}$ dimension $0$ in mass units; the ghost $c$ has dimension $0$, the antighost $\bar c$ and auxiliary field $b$ have dimension $2$, and the BRST differential has dimension $0$. Assign each antifield the dimension making its product with the corresponding BRST variation have density dimension $4$. The model postulate supplies the physical units, bundle sector, action, and boundary conditions; the classical gauge-invariance result supplies invariance under the declared bundle gauge transformations. This definition does not prove either supplier.

In the chosen local trivialization write $D_\mu c=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$ and choose the linear covariant gauge condition $G(A)=\partial^\mu A_\mu=0$ with gauge parameter $\xi>0$. The nonminimal BRST variables are an odd antighost $\bar c$ of ghost number $-1$ and an even auxiliary field $b$ of ghost number $0$, with $s\bar c=b$ and $sb=0$. The gauge-fixing fermion and gauge-fixing contribution are

$$\Psi_\xi=\int d^4x\,\kappa(\bar c,\partial^\mu A_\mu+\tfrac{\xi}{2}b),\qquad S_{\rm gf}:=s\Psi_\xi.$$

Here $s$ is the odd BRST derivation on the finite-jet field algebra, extended to the nonminimal variables and their antifields using the specified BV convention. The gauge condition is a local perturbative choice; it does not assert a global slice or remove all gauge copies. A finite-dimensional regulated configuration space has an ordinary Faddeev–Popov Jacobian only when it supplies the finite-dimensional group action, gauge condition, and transverse slice data in the preceding finite-dimensional definition. Such a Jacobian is not a continuum functional determinant and does not define a continuum measure.

A **formal perturbative renormalization datum** consists of the selected pure SU(2) classical BV action $\Gamma_0$, the above gauge-fixing choice, the dimensional-regularization prescription $D=4-2\epsilon$, modified minimal subtraction of the $1/\epsilon$ poles together with $-\gamma_E+\log(4\pi)$, and a local counterterm space $\mathcal C_{\leq d_*}$. Here $d_*$ is a finite engineering-dimension bound fixed by the selected power-counting prescription; $\mathcal C_{\leq d_*}$ consists of integrated Lorentz-scalar polynomials of ghost number zero and engineering dimension at most $d_*$ in $A,c,\bar c,b$, their antifields, and finitely many spacetime derivatives. The usual renormalizable four-dimensional Yang–Mills choice is $d_*=4$. The minimal BV action is the extension of $S_0$ by the antifield couplings to $sA_\mu=D_\mu c$ and $sc=-\tfrac12[c,c]$; when the nonminimal pair is included it also has the term $-\int_U\bar c^*b$. The datum is admissible only when $\Gamma_0$ satisfies the classical master equation and the chosen local BV functional domain has no nonzero central element of ghost number one. Its loop-counting variable $\lambda$ is formal and dimensionless; a formal effective action is a coefficient sequence $\Gamma(\lambda)=\Gamma_0+\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda^n\Gamma_n$ and no convergence at any nonzero $\lambda$ is asserted.

For a local BV functional $\Gamma$, define the Slavnov functional by $\mathfrak S(\Gamma):=\tfrac12(\Gamma,\Gamma)$ using the chosen odd antibracket, and define the linearized operator $B_{\Gamma_0}X:=(\Gamma_0,X)$. The datum has the **local QAP property** when, at each first order $n$ where the coefficientwise Slavnov identity fails, its defect has a finite-jet local four-form representative $\delta_n$ of ghost number one and a finite-jet local three-form $\rho_n$ of ghost number two satisfying

$$\mathfrak S(\Gamma^{(<n)})=\lambda^n\int_U\delta_n+O(\lambda^{n+1}),\qquad B_{\Gamma_0}\delta_n+d_H\rho_n=0.$$

This local representative and consistency condition are part of the QAP input; take $\delta_n$ to have engineering dimension at most $d_*$ and $\rho_n$ at most $d_*-1$. The definition does not prove the QAP. The finite-jet local BRST cohomology $H^{g,p}(s\mid d_H)$ uses the local forms, ghost grading, and horizontal differential of the preceding cohomology definition; $d_H$-exact top forms are identified with zero only under the declared compact-support or boundary condition. The coefficientwise Slavnov–Taylor identity is $\mathfrak S(\Gamma(\lambda))=0$ as an equality of formal power series.

items.physical_scope: Formal coefficientwise Slavnov–Taylor identities for the adopted pure SU(2) Yang–Mills perturbation theory, conditional on the QAP and local anomaly exactness; no continuum measure, convergence, nonperturbative existence, or empirical prediction is asserted.
items.statement:
In the axiom base inherited from the adopted model, fix the classical pure $SU(2)$ Yang–Mills model on oriented, time-oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, its selected smooth right-principal bundle sector $P\to M$, no matter fields, invariant form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, and fixed $g_{\rm YM}>0$. Let $U\subset M$ be a nonempty local trivialization chart, use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, and use the right-action curvature convention $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$. The adopted local classical action density is $-\kappa(F_A\wedge *_\eta F_A)/(2g_{\rm YM}^2)$. The local gauge potential $A_\mu$ is even with ghost number $0$ and engineering dimension $1$; the odd ghost $c$ has ghost number $1$ and dimension $0$. Define $D_\mu c=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$ and the minimal BRST transformations $sA_\mu=D_\mu c$, $sc=-\tfrac12[c,c]$. When the nonminimal pair is included, let $\bar c$ be odd with ghost number $-1$ and dimension $2$, and $b$ even with ghost number $0$ and dimension $2$, with $s\bar c=b$ and $sb=0$. Antifields have the opposite field parity and ghost number $-1-\operatorname{gh}(\Phi)$, with engineering dimensions chosen so $\Phi^*s\Phi$ has density dimension $4$.

Use the canonical BV antibracket and let the classical BV functional be the pure-gauge extension
$$\Gamma_0=S_0+\int_U d^4x\left(A^{*\mu}_a(D_\mu c)^a+\tfrac12c^*_a[c,c]^a-\bar c^*_ab\right),$$
where the nonminimal term is omitted if that pair is not included, and $S_0$ denotes the adopted classical action on the chosen domain. Assume $\Gamma_0$ is even, has ghost number zero, satisfies $\tfrac12(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_0)=0$, and the chosen local BV functional domain has no nonzero central element of ghost number one. The model postulate and its classical gauge-invariance theorem are explicit inputs fixing and interpreting $S_0$; neither is proved by this theorem.

Choose the local Lorenz gauge $\partial^\mu A_\mu=0$ with constant $\xi>0$, dimensional regularization $D=4-2\epsilon$, modified minimal subtraction of $1/\epsilon$ poles together with $-\gamma_E+\log(4\pi)$, and a finite engineering-dimension bound $d_*$. The allowed counterterms are integrated Lorentz-scalar finite-jet polynomials of ghost number zero and dimension at most $d_*$ in $A,c,\bar c,b$, their antifields, and their spacetime derivatives. The formal loop variable $\lambda$ is dimensionless; $\Gamma(\lambda)=\Gamma_0+\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda^n\Gamma_n$ is a formal coefficient sequence with no convergence at nonzero $\lambda$ asserted. Write $\Gamma^{(<n)}$ for a partial action whose coefficients below order $n$ already satisfy the Slavnov identity.

Assume the local quantum action principle (QAP): at each first failing order $n$ there are a local ghost-number-one four-form $\delta_n$ of engineering dimension at most $d_*$ and local ghost-number-two three-form $\rho_n$ of dimension at most $d_*-1$ such that
$$\mathfrak S(\Gamma^{(<n)})=\lambda^n\int_U\delta_n+O(\lambda^{n+1}),\qquad B_{\Gamma_0}\delta_n+d_H\rho_n=0,$$
where $\mathfrak S(\Gamma)=\tfrac12(\Gamma,\Gamma)$, $B_{\Gamma_0}X=(\Gamma_0,X)$, and $d_H=dx^\mu D_\mu$ is the horizontal differential on finite-jet local forms. Assume local anomaly cancellation in the explicit form of a supplied sequence of allowed ghost-number-zero four-forms $\Xi_n$ and ghost-number-one three-forms $\Theta_n$ satisfying
$$\delta_n=B_{\Gamma_0}\Xi_n+d_H\Theta_n$$
at every first failing order; put $\Xi_n=\Theta_n=0$ at nonfailing orders. Compact support or the model's boundary conditions make the integral of each $d_H$-exact four-form vanish. Then the counterterm series $C(\lambda)=-\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda^n\int_U\Xi_n$ yields $\mathfrak S(\Gamma(\lambda)+C(\lambda))=0$ coefficientwise.

For $g\in\{0,1\}$, restrict $H^{g,4}(s\mid d_H)$, with $s=B_{\Gamma_0}$, to local cocycles of engineering dimension at most $d_*$; identify two allowed representatives when their difference is $sm+d_Hn$ for local forms of the indicated ghost numbers and the difference remains in the allowed power-counting space. The resulting ghost-number-zero quotient is exactly the local counterterm freedom modulo trivial counterterms and total derivatives. The ghost-number-one quotient classifies local obstruction classes in that space; a nonzero class cannot be removed by an allowed local counterterm. This is a quotient statement and asserts no finite basis of representatives. The conclusion is conditional on the local QAP and supplied anomaly-cancellation sequence; it proves neither premise and asserts no empirical result, continuum functional measure, convergence, or nonperturbative existence. Any finite-dimensional Faddeev–Popov Jacobian remains the ordinary Jacobian of its specified regulated group action and transverse slice; it is not a continuum functional determinant.

items.title: A Finite Orbit with Two Gauge-Condition Intersections
items.physical_scope: A finite-dimensional regulated gauge-orbit example only; it is not a non-Abelian Yang–Mills field theory or a continuum functional measure.
items.statement:
Let $X=\mathbb R^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}$ have positive density $|dx\,dy|$, and let $K=S^1$ have angle coordinate $\theta$ and right-invariant density $|d\theta|$. Let $K$ act on the right by
$$(x,y)\cdot e^{i\theta}=(x\cos\theta-y\sin\theta,x\sin\theta+y\cos\theta).$$
For $r>0$, set $s_r=(r,0)$, choose an open neighborhood $U_r\subset\{x>0\}$ of $s_r$, let $S_r=U_r\cap\{y=0\}$ have density $|dx|$, and set $\chi(x,y)=y$ on $U_r$. The unit angular generator $1\in\mathfrak k=T_eK\cong\mathbb R$ has infinitesimal orbit vector
$$R_{s_r}(1):=\left.\frac{d}{d\theta}\right|_{0}(s_r\cdot e^{i\theta})=(0,r).$$
The Faddeev–Popov operator is the linear map $M_{s_r}:=d\chi_{s_r}\circ R_{s_r}:\mathfrak k\to\mathbb R$, and its density Jacobian relative to $|d\theta|$ and $|dy|$ is $\Delta_{\rm FP}(s_r)=|\det M_{s_r}|=r>0$. The full orbit $K\cdot s_r$ nevertheless meets the global condition $y=0$ at both $(r,0)$ and $(-r,0)$. Thus the local nonzero Jacobian proves transversality near $s_r$ but does not select one global representative for the orbit. The regulator group $K$ in this finite-dimensional toy is not identified with the model's non-Abelian structure group $G$.

items.physical_scope: A local formal Lorenz-gauge functional in the finite-jet Yang–Mills BRST algebra; no global slice, continuum measure, or empirical prediction is asserted.
items.statement:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ be a nonempty open region with compact support or boundary conditions that remove total-derivative terms. Work in the adopted pure $SU(2)$ model, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and normalized positive $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, extended bilinearly to the graded coefficient algebra. In the finite-jet algebra take $A_\mu$ to be an even $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued field of ghost number $0$ and dimension $1$, $c$ an odd $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued field of ghost number $1$ and dimension $0$, $\bar c$ an odd $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued field of ghost number $-1$ and dimension $2$, and $b$ an even $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued field of ghost number $0$ and dimension $2$. Let $\xi>0$ be dimensionless. Use the Lie-algebra bracket and odd left BRST derivation

$$sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c],\qquad sc=-\tfrac12[c,c],\qquad s\bar c=b,\qquad sb=0,$$

extended to jets by commuting with total derivatives. Define the Lorenz-gauge fermion and its BRST-exact functional by

$$\Psi_\xi=\int_U d^4x\,\kappa(\bar c,\partial^\mu A_\mu+\tfrac{\xi}{2}b),\qquad S_{\rm gf}:=s\Psi_\xi.$$

Then

$$S_{\rm gf}=\int_U d^4x\,\left(\kappa(b,\partial^\mu A_\mu)+\tfrac{\xi}{2}\kappa(b,b)-\kappa(\bar c,\partial^\mu D_\mu c)\right),\qquad D_\mu c:=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c],$$

is a local, even, ghost-number-zero functional of density dimension $4$, and it is BRST-closed. It is an exact gauge-fixing term in the formal local algebra; this example does not claim a global representative for every gauge orbit or a continuum functional measure.
